name: STILL LIFE WITH CORPONATION — Augmented Reality Vanitas Seri
subcategory: augmented reality mural / AR public art
creator: Nneka Uzo-Marchetti, licensed muralist, later operating as unlicensed after permit revocation
description: An augmented reality mural series overlaying classical vanitas still life compositions onto the exteriors of corponation headquarters throughout GLMZ — visible only through BCI AR filters or unlicensed lens overlays, each composition precisely referencing a specific historical painting tradition (Dutch Golden Age, Mughal miniature, Aztec codex, Song dynasty) but replacing traditional vanitas symbols with the corponation's actual assets: patent portfolios as hourglasses, market share as rotting fruit, executive compensation as skulls. Seventeen installations completed before Uzo-Marchetti's AR publishing license was revoked.
medium: augmented reality / BCI AR overlay / unlicensed lens filter
cultural_impact: The series demonstrated that AR art could function as invisible protest infrastructure — visible to those with the filter, invisible to those without, existing in the same space simultaneously as the corporate branding it critiques.
controversy: After permit revocation, Uzo-Marchetti released the filter source code publicly; hundreds of unauthorized copies now circulate, some modified to target additional buildings. She faces ongoing civil litigation from four corponations.
story_hooks: A character using the AR filter to view a STILL LIFE installation notices a seventeenth piece has appeared on a building Uzo-Marchetti never worked on — and the composition contains information that couldn't be public.
Uzo-Marchetti is offered full license reinstatement and dropped litigation in exchange for transferring ownership of the filter code to a corponation that wants to study how it works.
Someone has modified the filter to display the vanitas imagery over individual people rather than buildings — and the targets seem to be chosen deliberately.
